A fallback for networks that pass little but DNS. The Xray config from client-config switches to it when the other transports fail.

ns.example.com.  A   <server IP>
t.example.com.   NS  ns.example.com.

Open 53/udp, then add --profile xdns to init, or:

sudo morzer config set installation.profile=xdns

If systemd-resolved holds port 53, set xdns_bind to the public IP.

items.title: A domain of its own
items.text:
Better: a resolver that flags tunnel queries blocks the domain above them, which would take the site with it. Use a cheap, unrelated domain (example.net) for nothing but the tunnel:

; at example.net's DNS provider
ns.example.net.  A   <server IP>
t.example.net.   NS  ns.example.net.

dig +short NS t.example.net                       # ns.example.net. once delegated
sudo morzer config set xdns_domain=t.example.net
sudo morzer task run client-config --output -- --full phone   # resend: the config names the zone

items.title: Install
items.text:
You need a domain, a Linux host outside the restricted network, and an upstream proxy. example.com stands for your domain throughout.

  1. DNS: point the domain at the server:

    example.com.  A  <server IP>

  2. Firewall: open 80/tcp and 443/tcp in the cloud provider's firewall (a VPC firewall rule, on some clouds). Docker's published ports bypass ufw and firewalld, so the provider's firewall is the one that counts. Allow SSH with keys only.

  3. Host: install Docker, sops, age and morzer, with bootstrap.sh on Debian or Ubuntu.

  4. Recovery key: it decrypts the backups. Make it, and keep it off the machine:

    morzer secret recipients generate-recovery-key ~/dotdash-recovery.key

    It prints the public half, age1…, which the next step takes.

  5. Deploy:

    sudo morzer init --release oci://ghcr.io/morzecrew/dotdash-server:stable \
  --domain example.com --recovery-recipient age1…
sudo morzer secret set upstreams    # socks5://user:pass@host:port, one per line
sudo morzer apply
    • upstreams lists the ways out, one per line, in order: socks5://, socks5+tls://, http:// or https:// and user:pass@host:port, or a WireGuard or OpenVPN exit's wireguard:// or openvpn:// line. The first that answers carries the traffic. See Upstreams for backups, IPv6, WireGuard and OpenVPN.
    • Changing proxy later is one secret edit upstreams and one restart.
    • init prints the release's signing key and trusts it. To check even this first release against the key published with the repository, add --signing-key "$(gh variable get MINISIGN_RELEASE_PUBKEY -R morzecrew/dotdash)".

  6. Check: apply succeeds only once Xray reaches the internet through the upstream and 443 serves the site with a trusted certificate. Later, at any time:

    sudo morzer doctor                        # health, and the failing layer if any
sudo morzer task run exit-check --output  # the exit sites see

Next: connect devices.

items.title: What leaks where
items.text:
• Traffic leaves only through the upstream. With the upstream down, clients get nothing, never this server's address. Xray has no route out; a gate container holds the upstream's credentials. Every apply, update and doctor checks this against what runs.
  • The upstream sees destination addresses, ports and volume, not hostnames: this server resolves them over DoH (dns_resolver), through the upstream. SNI stays visible unless the client uses ECH. resolve=upstream hands the upstream the hostnames.
  • On the device, only the app keeps traffic inside a dropped tunnel (TUN with a kill switch, or Android's "block connections without VPN"). A browser IP checker showing an IPv6 address that exit-check calls unavailable sees the device's own: route IPv6 into the tunnel or turn it off in the app.
  • To keep IPv6 out altogether, set ipv6=block where it applies: on a client it is refused on the machine, on a relay it ends there, and here no IPv6 destination leaves (parameters).

items.title: mKCP
items.text:
A link over UDP on its own port (kcp_port, 8447), for a network that blocks the TCP transports but lets UDP through. mKCP has no TLS underneath: its packets are encrypted under the kcp_seed secret and start with a fake header (kcp_header), so they look like neither KCP nor TLS. VLESS Encryption still protects what they carry. Open the UDP port in the provider's firewall, then:

sudo morzer config set installation.profile=mkcp   # with the DNS tunnel: xdns,mkcp

Each device gets a phone [kcp] link and an outbound in the Xray config.

  • Clients: v2rayN and v2rayNG. mihomo has no mKCP: it treats the link as TCP, which never answers, and its health check skips it. sing-box apps can't use it either.
  • kcp_header: dtls by default: each packet starts as a DTLS 1.2 record, as WebRTC calls and some VPNs send. wireguard starts it as WireGuard data; utp and wechat as those; srtp is Xray's own, which doesn't start as real RTP does; none sends bare encrypted packets. No header is known to pass everywhere: if one is blocked, try another, then let devices refresh their subscription or send them new links.
  • Bandwidth: mKCP resends lost packets eagerly, so on a lossy line it uses more than TCP would. The Xray config picks it, as any other link, whenever it answers fastest.

Off: set the previous profile (xdns) or sudo morzer config unset installation.profile, before any rollback to a release without it.

items.title: Moving to a new server
items.text:
Prepare: keep the recovery key off the machine, add a backup target, and set the A record's TTL to 300 s or less. Devices keep their links.

# on the new server, after bootstrap.sh
sudo morzer --product dotdash installation import --from-backup \
  --target s3://bucket/dotdash --credentials-file ./bucket.yaml \
  --identity ~/dotdash-recovery.key
sudo morzer update oci://ghcr.io/morzecrew/dotdash-server:stable
# optional, keeps Caddy's certificate (import prints both ids)
sudo morzer backup fetch <backup id>
sudo morzer restore --force --confirm <installation id> --identity ~/dotdash-recovery.key

Then point example.com (and ns.example.com) at the new IP and shut the old machine down: two live servers with one installation id confuse each other's backups.

items.title: Operations
items.text:
Updates, alerts, backups and doctor work the same on relay, client and canary machines; only the update channel names another bundle.

Task Command Update by hand sudo morzer update --stage && sudo morzer update --to <version> New morzer sudo morzer self-update Backups off the machine sudo morzer backup target add s3://bucket/dotdash --credentials backup_s3 Alerts sudo morzer notify target add https://hooks.example/morzer Health and faults sudo morzer doctor Which exit sites see sudo morzer task run exit-check --output Whether each CDN is refused subscriptions sudo morzer task run cdn-check --output Metrics for Prometheus sudo morzer config set metrics.textfile=/var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter

items.title: Unattended updates
items.text:
From :stable, nightly at 03:30.

Warning

This gives whoever holds the release key root on the machine.

sudo morzer config set update.check=true
sudo morzer config set update.channel=oci://ghcr.io/morzecrew/dotdash-server:stable
sudo morzer config set update.auto_apply=true

items.title: Managed from elsewhere
items.text:
A machine can follow an authority, an operator key that publishes what it should hold, as morzer describes it. Each bundle names what an authority may set; everything else stays the machine's own.

Bundle An authority may set It tells the authority (facts) server vless_clients, the shared keys (reality_key, vless_seed, reality_short_id, xhttp_path, kcp_seed, subscription_key), servers, relays, cdn_hosts, pools, subscription, direct its domain and ports, the REALITY public key and the VLESS encryption string relay vless_clients, dotdash_id, dotdash_encryption, dotdash_short_id, dotdash_servers, dotdash_address, dotdash_port, dotdash_public_key, ipv6 its relay-entry line, at entry_host canary every dotdash_* nothing client subscription_url, proxy_password nothing

The upstreams stay each server's own. A relay's facts carry the short id, and with own-site or mkcp the XHTTP path or the mKCP seed: the credentials its devices' links carry anyway. sudo morzer task run facts --output prints them.

items.title: Pin the exit IP
items.text:
doctor fails when the provider moves you:

sudo morzer config set probe_url=https://api.ipify.org 'probe_expect=^203\.0\.113\.7\s*$'

items.title: What the checks say
items.text:
• Alerts cover failed applies, updates and backups, and each morning's doctor, which names the failing layer: the proxy's address, its credentials, the destination, or the exit.
  • exit-check: "IPv6 unavailable" means the upstream has no IPv6 exit, which is not a leak. "MISMATCH" means IPv4 and IPv6 leave from different networks.
  • Backups run nightly: secrets, encrypted to the recovery key, and Caddy's certificates. See morzer's operating docs.

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Name Default upstream_mode failover how the upstreams lines share the traffic: failover (the first that answers), fastest or balance upstream_pin none the name= of the line that goes first; under ipv6=separate, a second name pins the IPv6 lines upstream_udp false carry UDP through the upstreams, every one of which must carry it (WireGuard, OpenVPN, SOCKS5 with UDP ASSOCIATE); otherwise dropped https_port 443 host port for REALITY and the site xdns_domain t tunnel zone (xdns); a name with no dot is under the domain xdns_bind 0.0.0.0 host address for UDP/53 xdns_mtu 900 tunnel reply size; lower it if replies get lost xhttp_reality_port 8443 port for XHTTP with REALITY; not https_port or 80 kcp_port 8447 UDP port for mKCP; not 53 with the DNS tunnel kcp_header dtls what mKCP's packets start with: dtls, srtp, utp, wechat, wireguard or none log_level error Xray error log; items.title: Secrets
items.text:
init generates every secret except the ways out, upstreams. Set it with sudo morzer secret set <name>, edit with sudo morzer secret edit <name>, replace a generated one with sudo morzer secret rotate <name>.

Name Generated upstreams no every way out, one per line, in order (Upstreams); required vless_clients yes one <uuid> [name] line per device vless_seed yes ML-KEM-768 seed the VLESS Encryption key pair derives from reality_key yes REALITY private key (x25519) reality_short_id yes REALITY short id clients present alongside the key xhttp_path yes secret path Caddy routes to Xray's XHTTP inbound subscription_key yes key the subscription URLs derive from kcp_seed yes key mKCP's packets are encrypted under

Rotating vless_seed, reality_key, reality_short_id or xhttp_path changes every link, and kcp_seed the mKCP links: resend them, or let subscriptions pick it up.

items.title: Several servers
items.text:
Same keys on every server, each under its own domain and the same https_port. Links then cover every server, and the Xray config fails over between them. Add and revoke devices on each.

# on the first server; sudo on b.example.com must not prompt
for s in vless_clients vless_seed reality_key reality_short_id xhttp_path; do
  sudo cat /run/dotdash/secrets/$s | ssh b.example.com sudo morzer secret set $s
done
# on every server
sudo morzer config set servers=example.com,b.example.com

items.title: Upstreams
items.text:
Every connection leaves through the ways out the upstreams secret lists: proxies, WireGuard exits and OpenVPN exits, one per line, in order. A change of provider, a backup or a second exit is one edit of that secret.

sudo morzer secret edit upstreams

# <url> [name=<name>] [group=<group>]
socks5://alice:secret@203.0.113.7:1080            name=isp-a
https://bob:secret@proxy.example.net:443          name=isp-b
wireguard://<private key>@198.51.100.4:51820?publickey=<base64>&address=10.34.0.3/32 name=home
openvpn://H4sIAAAAAAACA…                          name=vpn
A line Way out socks5://[user:pass@]host:port a SOCKS5 proxy socks5+tls://[user:pass@]host:port a SOCKS5 proxy over TLS http://[user:pass@]host:port an HTTP proxy https://[user:pass@]host:port an HTTP proxy over TLS wireguard://… a WireGuard exit, from its wg-quick file (below) openvpn://… an OpenVPN exit, from its client config (below)
  • After the scheme, a proxy is user:pass@host:port, or host:port with no login. The password may contain : and @, and is not percent-encoded. An IPv6 host goes in brackets.
  • name= is optional, lowercase letters, digits and dashes. doctor and the gate's log name each line by it, and upstream_pin takes it.
  • Blank lines and # lines are skipped.

Proxies with residential exits suit this best. With every line down, devices get nothing, never the server's own address: what leaks where.

items.title: Order and modes
items.text:
The gate probes every line through it, fetching probe_url, every 30 seconds, so every line sees that URL's host name; with resolve=gateway, clients' destinations still reach them as addresses. upstream_mode decides how the lines that answer share the traffic:

upstream_mode failover (default) the first line while it answers, so the exit stays put; when it doesn't, the fastest of the rest, and back to the first once it answers again fastest whichever line answers fastest balance every line that answers, each connection to any of them
  • A failed line moves connections within about a minute. Connections open at that moment break, and apps reconnect.
  • The exit changes with the line. Lines in one country keep geolocated sites behaving the same. Under balance, one site may see several exits in a session, which some sites answer with a captcha or a new login.
  • sudo morzer config set upstream_pin=isp-b puts that line first whatever its place, the others behind it as the mode has them; none (the default) keeps the file's order.
  • doctor passes while any line carries. exit-check shows the exit in use. If you pin the exit IP, match every line's address to stay quiet when another carries, such as 'probe_expect=^(203\.0\.113\.7|198\.51\.100\.9)\s*$'.

items.title: IPv6
items.text:
ipv6 decides where IPv6 destinations go:

ipv6 allow (default) through the lines like any other: right when every line has IPv6 separate through the lines marked group=ipv6, with upstream_mode applying to them alone, and never through the others block nowhere: names resolve to IPv4 only, so dual-stack sites still work over IPv4

A proxy carries IPv6 when its own host has it. A WireGuard exit does when its address holds an IPv6 address and its exit routes IPv6, and an OpenVPN exit when its server pushes IPv6. For IPv4-only proxies and a provider's separate IPv6 one:

socks5://alice:secret@203.0.113.7:1080        name=isp-a
socks5://alice:secret@[2001:db8::7]:1080      name=isp-a6 group=ipv6

sudo morzer config set ipv6=separate
sudo morzer task run exit-check --output

Destinations with an IPv6 address, dual-stack ones included, leave through the IPv6 lines, the rest through the others, and neither falls back to the other. A dual-stack WireGuard exit can serve both: group=upstream,ipv6. separate needs resolve=gateway (the default); two providers show as MISMATCH in exit-check, as expected.

items.title: WireGuard
items.text:
The wireguard-line task turns a wg-quick file, as a router or a provider exports it, into its line:

sudo morzer task run wireguard-line --output --input conf=./wg0.conf

wireguard://oIpc…%3D@vpn.example:51820?publickey=n9B5…%3D&address=10.34.0.3%2F32&allowedips=0.0.0.0%2F0%2C::%2F0&keepalive=25
  • Add it to upstreams, with a name= if you like. The line holds the private key: treat it as the file.
  • One [Peer] per line: a file with several needs splitting first.
  • The gate runs Xray's own WireGuard, on its built-in network stack, so it needs no extra privilege. DNS, PostUp and the like are left out: this server resolves names itself and runs no scripts.
  • A link an app shares works too: wireguard://<key>@host:port?publickey=…&address=…, with mtu, presharedkey, keepalive and allowedips (all of 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 unless given).

items.title: OpenVPN
items.text:
Up to 8 OpenVPN exits, one per line. They run in a container of their own, which the openvpn profile adds, each tunnel on its own device. A line holds the exit's client config, with its keys inline (<ca>, <cert>, <key>, <tls-crypt>), and a provider's login goes inline too:

<auth-user-pass>
user
password
</auth-user-pass>

The openvpn-line task turns the config into its line:

sudo morzer task run openvpn-line --output --input conf=./client.ovpn

openvpn://H4sIAAAAAAACA0vOyUzNK-HlSkktUygpzePl…

Before an update from a release without the task, make it by hand:

printf 'openvpn://%s\n' "$(gzip -c client.ovpn | base64 -w0 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=')"

Add the line, then turn the profile on. Until then the line leads nowhere and the other lines carry the traffic:

sudo morzer secret edit upstreams                       # add the line, with name=vpn if you like
sudo morzer config set installation.profile=openvpn    # with others, all of them: xdns,openvpn
sudo morzer task run exit-check --output
  • The line holds the keys: treat it as the config.
  • Before OpenVPN starts, its container's default route is replaced by routes to the servers in the configs, so nothing leaves around a tunnel, even while it connects. No tunnel takes a default route: each line's traffic leaves through its own tunnel alone, and goes nowhere while that tunnel is down. Every apply and doctor checks that the container has no default route around the tunnels.
  • It runs as root with NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun, the one container here that does: OpenVPN takes nothing less. It reads its lines from the upstreams secret, which is the gate's, with DAC_READ_SEARCH.
  • An edit of upstreams restarts it, and every tunnel with it. If an OpenVPN exits, it starts again within a minute, and nothing leaves through it while it is down; the other tunnels carry on.
  • A config can't run scripts, or send OpenVPN's log anywhere but docker logs. The servers' addresses are looked up when the container starts: a provider that moves its server is reached again after sudo morzer restart vpn.
  • The server's kernel must be Linux 5.7 or newer, which lets the SOCKS hop beside the tunnels send each line's traffic into its own tunnel without privilege.
  • To drop them, turn the profile off, then remove the lines. The other way round, the container restarts with no line to run, and refuses.

Exits must be outside the restricted network

WireGuard and OpenVPN are easy to detect and block. Between this server and an exit outside that doesn't matter; an exit inside the restricted network would be blocked, and would send the traffic back where it came from.

items.title: UDP
items.text: upstream_udp=true carries devices' UDP, such as calls and QUIC, through the lines. Every line must carry it then: a WireGuard or OpenVPN line, or a SOCKS5 proxy with UDP ASSOCIATE; an HTTP proxy drops it. Off, UDP is dropped here and apps fall back to TCP.

items.title: What doctor says
items.text: When nothing gets out, doctor asks the first lines directly and names each by its name=: one that doesn't answer, one that refused the credentials in its line, a WireGuard peer that didn't carry it, an OpenVPN tunnel that is down. A line that answers when asked directly points at the gate instead.

items.title: XHTTP with REALITY
items.text:
A third link on its own port (xhttp_reality_port, 8443), for a network that passes another port better than 443. Xray-core clients (v2rayN, v2rayNG) and mihomo. Open the port in the provider's firewall, then:

sudo morzer config set installation.profile=xhttp-reality   # with the DNS tunnel: xdns,xhttp-reality

Off: set the previous profile (xdns) or sudo morzer config unset installation.profile, before any rollback to a release without it.
